concept: Jito tips and bundles and block engine
summary: Source-anchored research for Jito tips and bundles and block engine. Run status: COMPLETED.

facts.text: A sendBundle success response means the Block Engine received the bundle, not that it landed. The result is a bundle ID (the SHA-256 of the transaction signatures). Users report a returned ID with nothing on Solscan. Check getInflightBundleStatuses (Pending, Landed, Failed or Invalid, last 5 minutes) and getBundleStatuses (null if not found or not landed). (medium confidence)

Uncled blocks can unbundle a bundle. When a leader's block is skipped, any party that received it can rebroadcast its transactions. Those transactions enter the normal banking stage, which ignores bundle atomicity and revert protection, so they can land or revert on chain individually. Jito's mitigations: add pre- and post-account checks, and keep the tip in the same transaction as the strategy so a failed transaction does not pay the tip. (low confidence)

Keep a second path. Jito's DBI notes say to keep the Block Engine as a fallback because DBI serves BAM leader slots only and pauses during BAM node maintenance. Jito planned to put every mainnet BAM node into Maintenance Mode before the Alpenglow upgrade, with DBI users told to use the legacy Block Engine path. RPC Fast describes production senders fanning out to several Block Engine regions plus other relays, with raw RPC as a degraded fallback. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-13)

Landing-probability folklore is unverified. A DEV Community post models landing probability as a logistic, steep between the 50th and 75th percentile of recent landed tips, but admits this shape is an assumption and not measured data. Troop Messenger's 34% to 81% acceptance-rate improvement is labelled by the article itself as a 'reconstructed case composite', so neither is evidence of real landing rates. (low confidence)

Blockworks Advisory says the Jito Block Engine, which drives tips, is used across 98% of Solana stake even though the Jito client family runs about 54%. It calls that reach a concentration point: a bug or outage in Jito-Solana could affect most of the network at once. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-08-10)

In early 2024 (March, per Helius) Jito discontinued its mempool stream. It gave searchers a roughly 200 ms preview of pending transactions, and searchers used it for sandwich attacks. Jito gave up revenue to stop it. (high confidence)

Jito tip income per block differs by validator client. Syndica's March 2026 data shows Agave Rakurai earning 250% more Jito tips per block than the typical validator and Frankendancer Jito Revenue 230% more. The break-even stake for profitable operation at 0% commission rose from 24k SOL (January 2025) to 87k SOL (February 2026) as tips and priority fees declined. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-04-27)

Claims that Jito tips dominate Solana fee flow are dated and unmethodical. Freya says tips were 66% of total fees plus tips in Q1 2025. RPC Fast says tips are 60%+ of priority-fee volume, up from about 10% in April 2023. Neither shows a method. Blockworks Advisory and Syndica report the mix moving away from Jito tips in 2026. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-07)

Syndica's March 2026 data show Rakurai and Harmonic variants earning more Jito tips per block than the typical validator (Agave Rakurai +250%, Frankendancer Jito Revenue +230%, Frankendancer Harmonic Performance +140%, Agave Harmonic +19%). This suggests that clients outside the Jito brand still receive Jito tip flow. No source read states whether Harmonic or Rakurai validators accept Block Engine bundles, so the stake that can process bundles may be larger than the Jito-branded client share. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-03-31)

A Jito bundle holds at most 5 transactions. They execute sequentially and atomically within a single slot: if any transaction fails, none commit, and a bundle cannot cross a slot boundary. Bundles are only forwarded to leaders running Jito-Solana. (high confidence)

A Jito bundle is a list of up to 5 fully signed transactions. They execute in the listed order, all-or-nothing, inside one slot. If any transaction fails, none of them commit, and a bundle cannot cross a slot boundary. (high confidence)

Users report the sendBundle error 'Bundle Dropped, no connected leader up soon'. Read literally, the Block Engine saw no connected Jito leader scheduled soon. Jito warns that tips do not prioritize transactions at validators that are not Jito-Solana leaders, so a tip aimed at such a slot is wasted. Jito's GitBook adds that bundles are not forwarded between validators. (medium confidence)

A Jito bundle is a list of up to 5 fully signed transactions that execute in the listed order, atomically and all-or-nothing, inside one slot. A bundle cannot cross a slot boundary. If any transaction fails, none of them commit. Jito presents this as MEV protection, fast landing and revert protection. (high confidence)

Block Engine endpoints: https://mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf (any region) plus amsterdam, dublin, frankfurt, london, ny, slc, singapore and tokyo subdomains of mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf. Bundles use /api/v1/bundles and single transactions use /api/v1/transactions. A UUID is optional, passed as the x-jito-auth header or a uuid query parameter. Send bundles in base64, because base58 is deprecated and slow. The default limit is 1 request per second per IP per region. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06)

Jito warns that skipped slots produce uncled blocks, and transactions from a bundle can be rebroadcast from them. Such rebroadcast transactions do not respect bundle atomicity or revert protection, so they can land and revert on-chain. Jito advises putting the tip inside the main transaction rather than a standalone tip transaction, and adding pre/post account checks. (low confidence)

BAM (Block Assembly Marketplace) moves transaction sequencing into AMD SEV-SNP TEE nodes that keep transactions encrypted until execution. Validators execute the pre-sequenced result, can fall back to their own TPU, and can run plugins for application-controlled ordering rules. Helius flags the risks as TEE vulnerabilities, node-operator censorship and centralization. It says MEV is relocated rather than eliminated. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-07-31)

Validators run Jito-Solana, a modified Agave client. Searchers, apps and bots send bundles and transactions to the Jito Block Engine over gRPC or JSON-RPC. The Block Engine forwards winning bundles to the current leader. Tips go to validators and their stakers after Jito's fee. Jito's GitBook adds that bundles are not forwarded between validators. (high confidence)

Jito serves JSON-RPC from a global mainnet Block Engine URL and from regional URLs for Amsterdam, Dublin, Frankfurt, London, New York, Salt Lake City, Singapore and Tokyo. Single transactions go to /api/v1/transactions (sendTransaction). Bundle methods use /api/v1, and sendBundle posts to /api/v1/bundles. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-05)

Jito's tipping practice: put the tip instruction in the same transaction as the main logic. If space is tight, put post-checks or assertions (slot check, balance check) in a separate tipping transaction. Avoid standalone tip transactions in bundles; Jito says they raise exposure to uncle bandit cases. Keep the tip accounts out of Address Lookup Tables. (low confidence)

Simulate before you send. Jito tells users whose bundle will not land to validate transactions with simulateTransaction and notes that a Jito-Solana RPC should support simulateBundle. Alchemy documents simulateBundle as simulating a bundle without paying a tip. (medium confidence)

Architecture: Jito-Solana is Jito's fork of the Solana (Agave) validator. A validator running it connects to a Jito Block Engine. Searchers, dApps and bots submit transactions and bundles to the Block Engine over gRPC or JSON-RPC. The Block Engine simulates bundles, picks the most profitable combination and sends it to the leader, which executes the bundles atomically and collects the tips. The tips are then redistributed to the validator and its stakers. (high confidence)
